newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt evacuates sick man from Libyan border camp.
newsitem.headline: Egypt evacuates sick man from Libyan border camp.

text.p: Egypt on Thursday evacuated a Palestinian from a desert camp on the border with Libya after he suffered a heart attack, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said.

A UNHCR spokeswoman said Egyptian Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi gave clearance for Jameel Mohamed Mostafa, 50, to be taken to a hospital in Mersa Matrouh, on Egypt's Mediterranean coast.
Earlier in October Cairo allowed a heavily pregnant woman, bleeding and in danger of dying, to enter Egypt from the camp where some 200 Palestinians have been stranded for more than a year.
The refugees were among thousands of Palestinians expelled by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi last year to expose what he sees as a hollow peace deal between their leaders and Israel.

Diplomats in Cairo said there were high-level contacts between Egypt, Libya, the Arab League and UNHCR that may allow the Palestinians to soon leave the camp, described by aid workers as a rubbish dump unfit for human habitation.
They did not elaborate but said the stranded Palestinians may be allowed to either return to Libya or enter Egypt.
Egypt has so far refused to let in the Palestinians unless they have travel documents to another country.
Under the terms of the peace deal between the Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel, the Jewish state controls the entry points to the Palestinian self-rule areas.
